summary: Eight compute-bound experiments completed in 84.1 wall-time minutes, averaging 11 minutes per experiment under disk-mtime reconstruction. The longest executions were 'Bind natural output annotations to complete answer sentences' at 25.38 minutes, 'Qualify real organic-visit controls through the scored ARC wrapper' at 20.75 minutes, and 'Bound hardware next steps by authenticated service evidence' at 15.52 minutes. Available timing records do not provide intra-task stage breakdowns, and the snapshot recorded GPU 1 active at 96% utilization with no evidence of multi-model concurrency.
bottlenecks_identified: The top three compute-bound experiments account for 61.65 of the 84.1 total wall-time minutes, but the timing record lacks intra-task stage measurements to isolate specific execution overheads.
Milestone wall time was reconstructed from disk modification times via fallback because the live git-log path found 0 commits, leaving task boundaries and granular phase receipts unrecorded.

The GPU monitor report provides a single point-in-time snapshot, which cannot evaluate active accelerator utilization across the 84.1 minutes of task execution, verify model concurrency, or substantiate batching behavior.
improvements_suggested: Persist structured execution receipts with monotonic start, completion, and intra-task phase timings to remove reliance on disk-mtime reconstruction.
Sample GPU utilization and memory throughout task lifespans, correlated with task and process IDs, to evaluate accelerator efficiency across entire runs.
Run a controlled benchmark evaluating inference request batching (8-16 queries per forward pass) against the single-question baseline before altering pipeline defaults.
Record concurrent model load declarations at task initiation to reliably determine DualGPURunner dispatch eligibility.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Add monotonic sub-phase timers and task-linked continuous GPU monitoring to experiment execution receipts.
Run a bounded batching benchmark for GGUF inference to evaluate throughput improvements within VRAM limits before modifying defaults.
Emit explicit task lifecycle timestamps and concurrent model count telemetry to verify DualGPURunner eligibility and avoid fallback timing reconstruction.
meta_reflection: The GPU monitor snapshot shows GPU 1 active at 96% utilization running llama.cpp while GPU 0 remains idle, which aligns with single-model inference rather than an unengaged DualGPURunner configuration. Because accelerator metrics were not monitored continuously across the 84.1 minutes and intra-task phase timings were omitted, internal bottlenecks cannot be isolated from available records. Estimated time savings remain 0% in the absence of counterfactual measurements evaluated against an established baseline.
